title: The route of a swap: which attention heads carry a swapped concept from the word to the answer?
written: 2026-10-16, before any run of route.py. Seen beforehand: exp118 (swaps at floor 8 move 95%/86% of facts), the tower's attention flows (heads.json). No head-level data on swaps has been looked at.
model: Qwen/Qwen3-4B, bf16, MPS (eager attention), concept_swap.py W edits at block 8, alpha 1 (exactly the site's engine)
why: Neuron-level maps failed shuffle tests (exp111), transcoder influence is diffuse (exp116), yet one vector moves a whole bundle (exp118). Test whether the bundle travels along a small, findable set of attention heads (a 'tract') or spreads over many.

items.prompt: chat template, no thinking: question + ' Answer in a few words.'; read at the last prompt position (the first answer token)
attributes_A: What language do most people in {X} speak?
attributes_B: What is a famous food from {X}?
What is a famous landmark in {X}?
items.inclusion: t_X, t_Y = first token of the model's greedy answer for X and for Y written in; drop the item if t_X == t_Y or if the swap effect E < 2 (logits). Counts reported.

measures.metric: m = logit[t_Y] - logit[t_X] at the read position
measures.blocking a head set S: run the swap again, but each head in S emits its CLEAN output (o_proj input slice from the unedited run) at every position. Blocked share B(S) = 1 - mean(E_S) / mean(E) over included items. Sanity: S = all heads gives B = 1 exactly (the swap can only reach the read position through attention).
measures.selection (attribution): per head: sum over positions of (clean - swapped head output) . d m / d(head output) in the swap run (one backward pass); summed over training items; the k most negative (most blocking) heads
measures.selection (attention picture): per head: value-weighted attention flow (attn_flow.py, what the tower draws) from the X mention into the read position in the swap run, summed over training items; the k largest
measures.control: layer-matched random heads: for each selected head a random other head on the same floor; 20 draws, mean

hypotheses.H1: Sparse route: on held-out pairs (test pairs, attributes A+B), the top 32 heads by attribution (2.8% of 1,152), selected on training pairs (A+B), block B >= 0.50, and layer-matched random 32-head sets block <= 0.15.
hypotheses.H2: Shared route: heads selected on attributes A only (training pairs) block at least 0.7x as much on attribute-B items (test pairs) as heads selected on B itself (training pairs), at k = 32.
hypotheses.H3: The tower's picture finds the route: the top 32 heads by attention flow from the mention block >= 0.5x as much as the top 32 by attribution (test pairs, A+B).

exploratory: k curve: B for k = 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 (attribution and random)
where the route sits: floors of the top heads, their heads.json kinds, and how much of each route head's flow into the read position comes straight from the mention vs from tokens in between
other concept families: country-selected top-32 heads applied to weekday and animal-sound swaps (does one tract carry every concept?)
greedy behaviour: share of items whose first answer token returns to t_X when the route is blocked
